dossier.public_summary: The 0.81-day dip matches the star's own spot-spin period with a very large brightness swing that looks like stellar variability folded into a transit shape, and its apparent depth changes dramatically between TESS sectors and even within the same pipeline and between individual transits. Together this points to spot modulation rather than a 3-Earth-radius planet on the target, despite the flat-looking dip and on-target location.

reasons.why: Dip period 0.808 d is exactly one times the star's spot period (0.807 d) with 43753-65724 ppm swing. Large phase-curve at the same period with chi2 633.4 strongly favours spot modulation beating to a transiting-like folded shape, not a planet.

reasons.why: Depth truly changes between sectors and even within a pipeline (QLP 1368/3852 vs SPOC 10698/17402 ppm). A planetary transit depth should be steady; the observed 10x variation disfavours a planet despite no single-sector calibration explanation.
